messages:
Sam T: opened PR #4620 to tighten up SOC2-oriented wording for audit exports and retention. Legal noticed we still say 'permanent storage' in a couple places and our examples include raw emails and epoch-ms timestamps. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4620 please @Priya (legal) for wording and @Lina D for snippet cleanup.

docs-bot: PR 4620 build: preview available https://preview.redwood.ai/docs/pr-4620 · lint ok :white_check_mark:

Priya (legal): thanks. please avoid 'permanent' phrasing unless we document explicit opt-in flows. prefer 'retention period' and state defaults. examples should not include plaintext PII (emails/phones). also add a short compliance reminder: 'Customers are responsible for downstream retention in their storage.'

Lina D: I can overhaul the examples. propose: (a) show a pseudonymized row for readability (user_id: 'anon-0001'), (b) include a tiny redaction helper for CLI/Python consumers, and (c) add a migration note for the timestamp format change.

Jordan L: FYI we switched exports from epoch-ms to ISO8601/RFC3339 last quarter. lots of customer parsers assumed epoch. please add tiny parsing examples for python and curl/jq. e.g.
```bash
# curl + jq to strip email and convert timestamp to RFC3339-aware string
curl -s "https://export.redwood.ai/1234" | jq 'map(.user_email=null, .ts |= .)'
```
and
```py
# python parse RFC3339
from datetime import datetime
s = '2025-07-14T15:20:30Z'
parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
```
This should reduce support tickets.

Sam T: good call. For the top-level paragraph, is this ok? "By default audit exports redact personal identifiers; customers may configure retention periods per their plan. Contact support for extended retention or legal holds."

Priya (legal): close. replace 'personal identifiers' with 'personal identifiers (e.g., email, phone)' and add: 'Customers must handle exported data in accordance with applicable laws and internal policies.' Also add a link to the Data Processing Addendum in the compliance page.

Lina D: I'll push a commit that: 1) replaces wording, 2) swaps sample rows to pseudonyms, 3) adds the jq + python parse examples, 4) creates /guides/migration/audit-export-timestamp.md with a short note about epoch->RFC3339, and 5) fixes the docs index anchor that was broken. Will also add a tiny redaction util example in python: 
```py
# simple redaction helper
def redact_record(r):
    r['user_email'] = None
    r['user_phone'] = None
    r['user_id'] = f"anon-{r.get('user_id')[-4:]}"
    return r
```
I'll tag @Maria R for a final docs copy-edit.

Maria R: thanks — will check anchors and snippet paths (examples/sdk/). small nit: make sure the migration page has a clear 'what changed' bullet list for ops teams.

Sam T: checklist before merge: (a) legal phrasing updated, (b) snippets replaced/pseudonymized, (c) migration note added, (d) index anchor fixed, (e) preview link updated. ping when ready and I'll merge. :thumbsup:
